title: A sniff test and a spoon
allegory: An SAE latent is one jar in a huge spice rack: its sniff test says how much of that spice is in the dish, its spoon adds exactly that flavour back, and any one dish uses only a few jars.
map: the model's activation vector at one hook point
the latent's encoder direction, plus a bias and a ReLU
the latent's activation, zero on most tokens
the decoder direction, scaled by the activation and added back
only a few jars per dish
sparsity: a small L0, a handful of latents active per token

chapters.name: Neurons are a jumble
chapters.note: this neuron fires on ... all of these?

cap.1: Look inside a model one neuron at a time and each reacts to a jumble of unrelated things. There are more ideas than neurons, so they share.
cap.2: Because of superposition, neurons are polysemantic. A sparse autoencoder rewrites a layer's activations as a sparse mix of many more directions; each one is a latent.
cap.3: Each SAE latent has an encoder vector (a detector) and a decoder vector (what it writes back). This film is about reading, trusting and using one latent.

cap.1: Picture a rack of thousands of jars. Each jar's sniff test says how much of it is in the dish, and its spoon adds exactly that flavour back.
cap.2: A latent is one jar: an encoder direction that detects its pattern in the activation, and a decoder direction that writes the pattern back. Most jars read zero on any token.
cap.3: Trained with reconstruction loss plus a sparsity penalty (L1, or JumpReLU/TopK variants), so only a few latents are non-zero per token while their sum rebuilds the activation.

cap.1: Each jar sniffs, and if the smell is strong enough it adds spoonfuls of its flavour. Add up every jar's spoonfuls and you get the dish back, nearly.
cap.2: Activation = ReLU of the encoder direction dotted with the input, plus a bias. Output = activation times the decoder direction, summed over latents, plus a decoder bias.
cap.3: Encoder and decoder differ: w must pick out one latent while rejecting interference from overlapping ones, so w_i is not simply d_i. Steering adds d_i, the direction it writes.

cap.1: To learn what one jar is for, look at the dishes where its sniff test reads highest and at the flavours its spoon adds. Then name it, carefully.
cap.2: A latent dashboard has five parts: top activating examples, activation density, top logits (decoder direction times W_U), a logit histogram, and an LLM-written explanation.
cap.3: Top logits are the latent's logit lens, d_i · W_U, with no forward pass. Cross-check on Neuronpedia with text you predict should, and should not, trigger it.

chapters.name: Latent, not feature

left.title: latent
lines: may be dead, dense or absorbed

chapters.verdict: A latent is a hypothesis about a feature, not proof of one.

cap.1: A jar's label is a guess. A jar might hold a blend, never get used, or quietly take over a smaller jar's job. The jar is not the flavour.
cap.2: ARENA keeps 'latent' (a direction in the SAE) separate from 'feature' (a property of the data). Calling a latent a feature assumes the very thing you should test.
cap.3: Watch for dead latents (never fire), dense ones (fire on over 1 token in 100, hard to interpret) and feature absorption, where a general latent swallows a specific one.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Golden Gate: turn it up and it talks

cap.1: One jar found Arabic script that no single neuron showed. Another, in a much bigger model, made it talk as if it were the Golden Gate Bridge when turned up.
cap.2: Latents are handles for reading and steering: find the one you care about, check its dashboard, then add its decoder direction to push that behaviour up or down.
cap.3: Scaling Monosemanticity: feature 34M/31164353 in Claude 3 Sonnet, clamped to 10x its max activation, made the model self-identify as the bridge. Latents make steering targeted.

coda.title: Three jars: slide the input from pattern A to pattern B and raise the threshold

caption.1: Slide the dish from pure A to pure B. Jar A fades as jar B wakes up, and jar C, sniffing for something else, stays silent. Then raise the threshold.
caption.2: Each curve is one latent's activation as the input blends two patterns. A high threshold makes latents pickier: at an even blend, both can go silent and the mixture is missed.
caption.3: Toy: decoders 120° apart, encoder = decoder, input (1-x)d_A + x·d_B, so a_i = ReLU(m·(u·d_i) - t). The threshold trades L0 against missed activations: the sparsity tension.

where_else: Steering by adding a latent's decoder direction to the residual stream
Direct feature attribution and attribution patching, which credit a behaviour to individual latents
Transcoders, whose latents stand in for an MLP's input-to-output map
Autointerp, where an LLM writes and scores an explanation for each latent

hamming.what: One entry in a sparse autoencoder's dictionary: an encoder direction that detects a pattern in a layer's activations and a decoder direction that writes it back.
hamming.when: When you want readable, steerable units instead of polysemantic neurons, at one chosen hook point.
hamming.why: Latents turn a tangle of neurons into handles you can inspect, attribute to and steer with, as long as you treat each name as a hypothesis to test.

object.title: The spice ledger
object.subtitle: A sentence down one side, six jars along the other: how hard each jar fires on each word (illustrative values).

cap.1: Each bar is how strongly one jar fires on one word. Most of the table is empty: each word uses only a few jars. That is sparsity.
cap.2: Rows are tokens, columns are latents, heights are activations. Illustrative values, not a real SAE.
cap.3: A sparse code: each row has L0 of two or three, and each latent fires on a coherent subset of tokens.

cap.1: From above: each jar has its own kind of word. The Arabic-script jar stays silent on English text, exactly as it should.
cap.2: Specificity is the point: a latent that fires only on its pattern is one you can name and trust further.
cap.3: Silence on off-distribution text is evidence for a narrow latent; test with inputs you predict should and should not activate it.

cap.1: Raise the threshold and weak firings vanish: sparser and cleaner, but detail like the capital-letter jar starts to disappear.
cap.2: A higher threshold (or stronger sparsity penalty) lowers L0 at the cost of reconstruction.
cap.3: The L1 coefficient or JumpReLU threshold sets the sparsity-reconstruction trade-off; sparser is not reliably more interpretable.

cap.1: Clamp the bridge jar high on every word: that is steering. In Claude 3 Sonnet, clamping the bridge feature made the model talk as if it were the bridge.
cap.2: Clamping sets a latent's activation high everywhere, so its decoder direction is written in at every position.
cap.3: Scaling Monosemanticity clamped feature 34M/31164353 to 10x its max activation; the model self-identified as the Golden Gate Bridge.

cap.1: The last column never fires on anything: a dead jar. It never gets feedback, so it is wasted space, not a slow learner.
cap.2: Dead latents get no gradient. Many dead latents with good loss usually means the dictionary is simply too big.
cap.3: No activation means no gradient to the encoder; resampling can revive some, but persistent deadness signals an oversized d_sae.

predict.q: An SAE latent has two vectors. Which one do you add to the residual stream to steer?
predict.why: The decoder direction is what the latent writes back; the encoder is only its detector.

predict.q: A latent fires on more than 1 token in 100. What is the worry?

options.t: It is dense and probably hard to interpret

predict.why: Dense latents smuggle non-sparse computation into the SAE and rarely have clean meanings.

predict.q: Every top example for a latent is Arabic script. Can you call it 'the Arabic feature'?

options.t: Only as a hypothesis until you test it
Yes, the top examples prove it

predict.why: A latent is a direction in the SAE; a feature is a property of the data. Test with text that should and should not trigger it.

object.where: Any learned dictionary: a detector for reading, a direction for writing, and a sparsity budget in between.
